story: A 24-rider breakaway formed after a hard-fought opening half of the stage. Romele attacked from the break before being joined by Sivakov and Camprubí. The trio reached the final Alto de Aitana with around 5 minutes on the peloton, but Decathlon CMA CGM rapidly reduced the gap. Sivakov dropped Camprubí with 10 km remaining, but was caught 4.5 km from the summit as Gall repeatedly tested the reduced group of GC contenders. Carapaz also tried to anticipate the favourites before leader Mas launched the decisive attack with 3 km to go. Only Oscar Onley could stay with the red jersey, while Roglič briefly came close to rejoining them before Mas accelerated again. Mas kept Onley behind him all the way to the line to take his first victory in nearly 4 years and strengthen his overall lead ahead of the first rest day.
